tracks.narration: A plain comparator chatters when a noisy input crosses the reference. How do you give it a backbone?
Take an op-amp and wire feedback from the output back to the plus input through a resistor divider. That's positive feedback — the opposite of what you used for an amplifier.

When the output is high, the divider pushes the plus input up — the trip threshold V T H climbs. When the output is low, V plus drops, and the threshold falls to V T L. Two different thresholds for the same circuit.

Now sweep the input slowly up then back down. The output sits low until V in passes V T H — only then does it snap up. On the way back, V in must drop all the way to V T L before it snaps back. Two thresholds, one loop, no chatter.
That gap is the hysteresis band. Any noise smaller than the band can't toggle the output — one clean edge per real crossing.
